families.name: VAN Series variable arc spray nozzles
HE-VAN high-efficiency variable arc spray nozzles

notes: Every number was transcribed from Rain Bird's own charts (text layer of the PDFs, parsed by script with row-count checks, plus visual spot checks of the MPR strip/FLT page and the R-VAN strip page). Each family's per-series chart PDF was cross-checked number-for-number against the same tables in Rain Bird's 2023 Domestic Landscape Irrigation Catalog (d42139, https://www.rainbird.com/sites/default/files/media/documents/2022-11/d42139_2023_dom_turf_catalog_v3_eng.pdf, pp. 15-35): VAN, HE-VAN, U-Series, MPR and R-VAN tables are identical in both. That catalog is the latest landscape catalog Rain Bird links (checked 2026-10-20); the 2026 'What's New' guide adds no spray nozzle or 1800 body changes beyond SQ patterns.

Fixed-arc nozzles (MPR, U-Series): rows hold the FULL-CIRCLE equivalent per the schema (H x2, Q x4). Rain Bird's F/H/Q flows are close to but not exactly proportional, e.g. 5F at 30 psi prints 0.41 gpm while 5H prints 0.20 (=0.40 full) and 5Q 0.10 (=0.40 full); 8F 1.05 vs 8H 0.52 (1.04) vs 8Q 0.26 (1.04); 10F 1.58 vs 10H 0.79 (1.58) vs 10Q 0.39 (1.56).

Adjustable-arc nozzles (VAN, HE-VAN, R-VAN adjustable): the charts print a separate table per arc setting. 'rows' is the full-circle equivalent taken from the largest printed arc: the 360 deg table as printed for 10/12/15/18-VAN and all HE-VAN; for 4/6/8-VAN (max arc 330 deg) the 330 deg gpm x 360/330; for R-VAN14/18/24 (max arc 270 deg) the 270 deg gpm x 4/3, rounded to 0.01. Those two cases are derived numbers, not printed ones. Each such nozzle also carries 'printedByArc' (an addition to the schema): every arc table exactly as printed, gpm for THAT arc, not scaled.

4-VAN, 6-VAN and 8-VAN flows are clearly NOT proportional to arc: e.g. 4-VAN at 30 psi prints 0.88 gpm at 330 deg (0.96 per full circle) but 0.29 at 90 deg (1.16 per full circle), and the chart's own precip rates differ by arc (5.78 vs 6.98 in/h square). 10-VAN is also uneven (360 deg 2.60 gpm, 90 deg 0.75 = 3.00 per full circle). For these, prefer printedByArc at the nearest arc. VAN 12/15/18, HE-VAN, U-Series and R-VAN are proportional to within rounding.

chartPrecip is the chart's own square / triangular (50% diameter-of-throw spacing) value at the reference psi: 30 psi for MPR, VAN, HE-VAN and U-Series (Rain Bird's 'optimum pressure'); 45 psi for R-VAN (Rain Bird's 'recommended operating pressure', the bold row). For adjustable nozzles it is the value printed with the largest arc's table (precip differs slightly by arc on VAN). For R-VAN strips the two columns are Rain Bird's 'straight-line spacing' and 'triangular spacing based on 50% overlap of throw', stored as square / triangle. The MPR 15 Strip Series chart prints no precip, so null.

Strip nozzles are in their own families with flow 'constant' (gpm as printed; there is no arc to scale). Their rows carry radiusFt null plus widthFt and lengthFt per pressure as printed (an addition to the schema), because the pattern size changes with pressure. The 'strip' object holds the size at the reference pressure (30 psi MPR, 45 psi R-VAN). Corner strips (15LCS, 15RCS, R-VAN-LCS, R-VAN-RCS) are stored as type 'end' with an added 'corner': 'left'|'right', since the schema's types have no corner; they are placed at the corner of the strip, not mid-end.

15CST and 15SST print identical numbers (4x26 to 4x30, 0.89 to 1.21 gpm). 9SST is printed in the 15 Strip Series table (30 deg trajectory heading). 15CST is labelled center strip in Rain Bird's model codes; its printed W x L is 4 x 30 at 30 psi.

MPR patterns: Rain Bird's current MPR chart (2020) and the 2023 catalog list only F, H and Q for the 5, 8, 10, 12 and 15 Series (plus 8H-FLT and 8Q-FLT). No TQ (270), T (120) or TT (240) MPR or U-Series nozzles appear in any current Rain Bird chart; the 2017 catalog says to use HE-VAN 'for specialty patterns (previously U-Series T, TT, TQ nozzles)'. So TQ/T patterns were not found and are not included.

U-Series: the chart notes 'Radius refers to recommended product spacing. Actual radii along arc may vary'. Labels are normalized to U-8F style; the chart prints both U-8H and U8H. U-8, U-12 and U-15 print the same radius and gpm as MPR 8, 12 and 15 Series (U-8 precip differs by 0.01-0.02); U-10 differs from MPR 10 (1.64 vs 1.58 gpm full circle at 30 psi).

R-VAN: chart rows run 30-55 psi; no trajectory is printed (null). Rain Bird: do not reduce the radius below 17 ft (R-VAN24/24-360), 13 ft (R-VAN18/18-360) or 8 ft (R-VAN14/14-360). Rain Bird recommends 45 psi (1800-P45 / SAM-P45 bodies); on a 30 psi PRS body read the 30 psi row. Rain Bird's charts note all nozzles were tested on 4 in pop-ups in zero wind.

MPR, VAN, HE-VAN and U-Series charts print 15-30 psi only; Rain Bird recommends 30 psi regulated (PRS) bodies for higher supply pressure. Radius reduction over 25% of normal throw is not recommended (spray charts).

Bodies: 1800 models from Rain Bird's 1800 Series product page (base 1802/1804/1806/1812; SAM 1804/1806/1812; PRS-30 1802/1803/1804/1806/1812; P45, SAM-PRS and SAM-P45 1804/1806/1812). The 1803 base model is listed only in the 2022 1800 Series tech spec (5 in body, 3 in pop-up), not on the current product page. PRS = 30 psi in-stem regulator, P45 = 45 psi, 'with inlet pressures of up to 70 psi'. Rain Bird says all its plastic spray nozzles (U-Series, HE-VAN, R-VAN, MPR, VAN) fit all 1800 bodies and the UNI-Spray 'accepts all Rain Bird nozzles', so every body lists every family.

UNI-Spray: US400 is the 4 in body; US408HE/US410HE/US412HE/US415HE are the same body shipped with an HE-VAN-08/10/12/15 pre-attached and US410/US412/US415/US418 with a 10/12/15/18-VAN pre-attached (nozzle still swappable). Not pressure regulated. A field-installed SAM check valve (USSAM) exists.

Not included: RD1800 series bodies (not in this group's list; same nozzles fit), 1800 'XPCN' nozzles, R-Series fixed rotary nozzles, SQ square-pattern nozzles, 5 Series MPR stream bubblers (5F-B/5H-B/5Q-B/5CST-B) and other bubblers, and all metric columns.
